label: Peplink EPX-M8-LW2C1F1 (EPX with LCD module, 6x LTE-A)
description: Peplink EPX (EPX-M8-LW2C1F1): the same 7-slot FlexModule chassis built as 4x 10G SFP+, 8x 1G RJ45 with PoE+ and 6 LTE-A modems - 4 of 7 slots used, 30 Gbps router, 330 W PoE+ budget.

poe.note: Current datasheet rev 2404-v15, EPX-M8 spec table: "PoE Output 8x 802.3at PoE+ Output" and "330W PoE+ Power Budget" - this build has exactly one EXM-8C, so 8 PoE+ ports all drawing on that ceiling. The module table prices the same EXM-8C at "15W (255W max. with PoE Output)" in rev EPX-201910-v7 and "15W (105W max. with PoE+ Output)" in the 2020 revision; those are per-module figures for the same module and they disagree, so the chassis figure is the one recorded.

notes:
Peplink EPX datasheet, ordering table (Product Code / Description) — the row this model is built from: 
  "EPX-M8-LW2C1F1  EPX with LCD Module, 4x 10G SFP+, 8x GE and 6x LTE-A (Worldwide)."
The same table names its Asia-Pacific twin EPX-M8-LP2C1F1 with an identical port census, so only the worldwide SKU is modelled here;
the region is a modem-band difference and no interface list records it (the same treatment the SDX Pro storage SKUs got).

The census decomposes into the datasheet's own FlexModules and the tech-spec sheet's slot count ("Module Expansion: Yes (7 slots for FlexModule Plus)"):
  1x EXM-4F  -> 4x SFP+ ports  (module table: "Interface 4x SFP+ Ports *", 11 W)
  1x EXM-8C  -> 8x 10/100/1000M Ethernet, capable of PoE+  (module table: "8x 10/100/1000M Ethernet Ports*, Capable of PoE+")
  2x EXM-3LTEA-W -> 6x LTE-A Cat-6 modems, 300/50 Mbps down/up, 6x SMA + 1x GPS per module
which is 4 modules in 7 slots (three FlexModule Plus positions stay empty) — the ordering table and the slot count agree, which is the check that the code decodes correctly.
The sister SKU EPX-M8-LW5C1F1 is the same build plus three LTE-A modules (7 slots used); EPX-M8-LW1C3F3 is 3x EXM-4F + 3x EXM-8C + 1x EXM-3LTEA (12 SFP+, 24 GE, 3 LTE-A).

PoE, and the one place the datasheet contradicts itself. Current revision 2404-v15 states, on the EPX-M8 spec table,
"PoE Output 8x 802.3at PoE+ Output" and "330W PoE+ Power Budget", which is exactly this build's one EXM-8C as well. The 2019 revision (ref EPX-201910-v7)
prices the same module as "15W (255W max. with PoE Output)" and footnotes "^ The EPX-8M can support a maximum of 2 modules delivering PoE";
the 2020 archived revision states the module as "15W (105W max. with PoE+ Output)". The chassis ceiling (330 W) and the module ceiling (105/255 W)
are different numbers for the same box, so the budget recorded here is the chassis figure the current datasheet prints and the module figures are quoted here rather than averaged.
For the 24-GE twin (EPX-M8-LW1C3F3) the same three statements conflict outright — 8 PoE ports per the chassis row, 3 PoE-capable modules per the module table, at most 2 per the v7 footnote —
so that SKU is deliberately not catalogued yet (issue #495 records it).

Other vendor figures used: Router throughput 30 Gbps; PepVPN/SpeedFusion 4 Gbps no-encryption and 4 Gbps 256-bit AES (2404-v15; the 2020 revision says 2 Gbps AES);
5000-20000+ recommended users; 4000 SpeedFusion peers; 1000 IPsec tunnels; 1024 VLANs; 2000 APs; "Serial Interface: No", "USB WAN: No", "Wi-Fi AP: No",
"External Storage via USB Port: Yes"; two AC inputs 100-240 V with two hot-swappable PSUs; 18.9 x 21.7 x 3.6 in / 480 x 550 x 90 mm; 31.3 lb / 14.2 kg without modules.
No console port is published, so none is modelled.

Sources: https://web.archive.org/web/20200421214219/https://download.peplink.com/resources/peplink_epx_datasheet.pdf (Peplink EPX datasheet, ordering table and FlexModule table) ; https://www.peplink.com/compare/tech-specs/epx.pdf (slot count, 30 Gbps, Serial/USB/Wi-Fi rows) ; https://download.peplink.com/resources/peplink_epx_datasheet.pdf (rev 2404-v15: port ranges, PoE budget, environmental) ; https://www.advantesco.com/assets/files/peplink_epx_datasheet.pdf (rev EPX-201910-v7: EXM-8C 255 W, 2-PoE-module footnote).
